top_creatures.label: Dusk-scaled wyrm king (boss)
top_creatures.why: Set apart by data: a size field of 5 and a 160 resize on both axes (the only such pair checked; not compared across all NPCs). Its breath branch is chosen from the target's quadrant (script branches for south-west, south-east, north-east, north-west). On-screen read not viewed.
top_creatures.keep: Oversized scale from the size and resize fields; breath direction chosen by where the target stands; a random pick among attack options each tick.
top_creatures.change: Palette and wing silhouette (not the donor look); add a visible wind-up before breath; name and drop table of our own.

top_creatures.label: Ember hound (single high-tier hound)
top_creatures.why: A high-tier hound (name and level field only; model, speed and animations not viewed or read). The name alone sets a fire mood.
top_creatures.keep: Quadruped silhouette; fire mood; high-tier placement.
top_creatures.change: Bony plating and a split tail instead of the donor body; our own sound kit. Pack behaviour not read, so do not copy it.

top_creatures.label: Rift stalker (three tiers)
top_creatures.why: Three demon tiers in one ladder (the level field steps up across the three blocks), with a portal effect in the effects table. Escalation by level is in the data; the visual step between tiers was not viewed.
top_creatures.keep: Three-tier ladder by level; portal arrival effect.
top_creatures.change: Crystal shards instead of horns; a portal colour of our own; the size step to be designed by us.

top_creatures.label: Region-dyed spider brood
top_creatures.why: Several spider blocks share one family name in different tiers and regions (names and level fields; the models were not checked to be shared). Cheap variety if the body is reused.
top_creatures.keep: Family of named variants by region and level; poison and ice variants as separate tiers.
top_creatures.change: Silk strands as a traversal hazard; a different leg count; palettes of our own.

top_creatures.label: Bone guard (armed ladder)
top_creatures.why: Undead blocks in four states by name: unarmed, armed, giant and mage. The armed state is a separate block, so the weapon read is in the data; the silhouette itself was not viewed.
top_creatures.keep: Armed versus unarmed as separate states; a giant step; a caster variant.
top_creatures.change: The mage version carries a floating orb, not a staff; its own bone palette.

top_creatures.label: Desert scorpion king
top_creatures.why: Four named tiers from small to king by level field (names and levels only; the body shape was not viewed).
top_creatures.keep: Ladder of named tiers from small to king; poison tier as a separate variant.
top_creatures.change: Tail shape and claw count; an original palette, not the donor's.

top_creatures.label: Frost queen (elite)
top_creatures.why: A named ice-tier elite on top of a warrior tier; the frost look carries the boss read.
top_creatures.keep: Named elite on a warrior base; frost mood.
top_creatures.change: Crown or cape silhouette of our own; a different frost palette.

top_creatures.label: Grave caller (summoner)
top_creatures.why: A caster that brings in a zombie ally. A summon is easy to read and gives a tell before the fight.
top_creatures.keep: Summon-an-ally pattern; a caster with a named summoned creature.
top_creatures.change: Summoned creature type and summon cue; a different hood and staff.
top_creatures.ref: data/src/scripts/_unpack/all.npc [necromancer] [invrigar_the_necromancer] [summonedzombie]. Summon logic not read: the necromancer script was not opened.

classes.name: Skill tracks (15)
classes.role: No character classes in the data. These are the 15 skill folders: agility, combat, cooking, crafting, firemaking, fishing, fletching, herblore, magic, mining, prayer, runecraft, smithing, thieving, woodcutting.
classes.mechanic: Each skill has its own configs and scripts folder.
classes.progression: Levels gate items and actions (levelrequire folder).

classes.name: Combat styles
classes.role: Six damage types and nine stances.
classes.mechanic: Damage types: stab, slash, crush, ranged, magic, melee. Stances: accurate, aggressive, defensive, controlled for melee; rapid and long-range for ranged; normal and defensive for magic.
classes.progression: Chosen per weapon through the combat style table.

classes.name: Prayers (15)
classes.mechanic: Strength and reflex boosts, rapid restore and heal, item protection, and protection from magic, missiles and melee.

classes.name: Races and factions (from NPC categories)
classes.role: Human citizens, guards, barbarians, pirates, Zamorak monks, black knights, dark wizards, ice warriors, chaos dwarves, gnomes and ogres (names only).
classes.mechanic: Faction read from NPC category and palette, not from class rules.

looks.label: Tiered projectile effect pairs
looks.technique: Each ammo tier has its own travel and launch effect, so the arrow trail reads by tier. Fire, ice and ogre arrows have their own pairs.

looks.label: Palette-swapped effects on one model
looks.technique: One effect model is reused in several colourways through palette pairs (source and destination entries). Used for shooting star and book of binding.

looks.label: Scaled effects
looks.technique: An effect is stretched on both axes through resize fields: a huge smoke puff and a tall flame wall.

looks.label: Per-effect lighting override
looks.technique: Ambient and contrast fields set the lighting on one effect, for example the enchant ring and stunned effects.

looks.label: Breath effects with named animation
looks.technique: Dragon breath effects are separate model and animation pairs: single fire, triple fire, ice and acid.

looks.label: Portal and whirlpool
looks.technique: Portal and portal-end effects, plus a whirlpool location effect; each is an alpha-blended model and animation pair.

looks.label: Glowing elemental orbs
looks.technique: Fire, water and air orbs are described as magic glowing orbs. The glow itself is not in the item fields read; check the model and effect pair before recreating.

looks.label: Trim and gold-trim variants
looks.technique: Gold trim is a variant tag on the item (desc says gold trim), not a shader. Reproduce as a tier variant with a rim highlight.

originals.name: Cinder Tyrant
originals.idea: A boss a head taller than the rest of the zone. Its breath turns toward whoever is closest on its side, and a clear wind-up tells the player where it will fire.
originals.keep: Oversized silhouette; breath chosen by quadrant; random pick between melee and breath.
originals.change: Palette (ember and slate, not the donor look); wing shape; a wind-up tell; our own name and drop table.

originals.name: Rift Stalkers
originals.idea: Three demon tiers that step out of one portal, each tier larger and more armoured.
originals.keep: Three-tier ladder; portal arrival; size escalation.
originals.change: Crystal shards instead of horns; a portal colour of our own.

originals.name: Region-dyed brood
originals.idea: One spider body in five region palettes; silk strands become a traversal hazard.
originals.keep: One body, many palettes; poison and ice tiers.
originals.change: Silk as a hazard instead of a plain enemy; leg count; palettes of our own.

originals.name: Bone guard ladder
originals.idea: An undead body in four states, where the armed state changes the silhouette most.
originals.keep: Armed versus unarmed silhouette; giant step; mage variant.
originals.change: The mage carries a floating orb, not a staff; a bone palette of our own.

originals.name: Oath plate
originals.idea: Three faction-coloured four-piece plate sets from one rune-tier shape.
originals.keep: One shape, palette swapped per faction; four pieces per set.
originals.change: Faction names and colours of our own; add a shoulder mark instead of a full recolour.

originals.name: Gilded trim ladder
originals.idea: Each metal tier has a trim variant and a gold-trim variant, so the top tiers gain a rim highlight.
originals.keep: Two variants per tier (trim and gold trim).
originals.change: The gold trim is a rim-light shader, not a palette swap.

originals.name: Tier trails
originals.idea: Ammo tiers each have their own launch and travel effect pair, so the trail itself tells the tier.
originals.change: Effect colour, sound cue and trail length of our own.

originals.name: Frontier depth bands
originals.idea: Danger rises one band every eight tiles from a start line, with a warning line before the first band.
originals.keep: Depth banding with a warning line.
originals.change: Band names, perks and the step size of our own.
